Subject: Exhibit E cap/floor language — initial redline

Connor —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our procurement team, CloudNova needs clearer protection on the pricing horizon and non‑retrospective caps. I attached our redline to Exhibit E (CloudNova_ExhibitE_redline_v3.pdf) and a clean pricing schedule export (Pricing_Schedule_3.xlsx) for reference. High level asks:

- Remove the automatic floor re‑calibration clause that triggers on monthly true‑ups; we need a stability window of at least one quarter.
- Cap increases tied to model upgrades should be limited to a 10% annualized band unless both parties agree to broader changes.
- We request a carve‑out for credits if latency SLOs are missed more than twice in a 90‑day period.

Can you circulate an internal redline and let us know which items Redwood can accept vs which need legal negotiation? We are targeting signature by end of May.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call next week.

Samantha Lee

Subject: Re: Exhibit E cap/floor language — internal review and proposed commercial position

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear redline and the timeline. I pulled together Redwood's commercial position after a quick sync with Revenue Ops and Product:

- Stability window: we can agree to a 90‑day stability window for floor recalibration on committed tiers. For burst/burst‑credit usage we need a 30‑day faster feedback loop (can we confirm typical burst patterns?).
- Model upgrade caps: we can commit to 10% annualized cap on list prices for the first year after GA for that model family; after that, price movement reverts to the standard quarterly review in Exhibit E.
- SLO credits: happy to include a credit mechanism for repeated SLO misses, but need the credit formula to be bounded (max liability = 2x monthly fees).

I'll loop in Legal to propose specific wording. Laura and Marissa — can one of you draft a concise redline that reflects the stability window and the cap guardrail above? I want to avoid overly prescriptive telemetry obligations in the contract.

Short call to align? I have a 30‑minute slot Wednesday 11:00–11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien

Subject: Re: Exhibit E cap/floor language — legal redline suggestions

Team —

I reviewed CloudNova's redline and Connor's commercial position. Key legal points to include (draft language suggestions below) — please treat these as starting points:

1) Stability window (floors): "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, any downward adjustment to the Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) or floor pricing for a given billing period shall not be effective until the expiration of a 90‑day Stability Period following notice to Customer, except where Customer has triggered burst overage thresholds as defined in Schedule A."

2) Model upgrade cap: "For any model upgrade that materially changes token throughput characteristics invoked by Customer, Redwood's list price adjustment for the upgraded model, if any, shall not exceed ten percent (10%) on an annualized basis measured from the Effective Date of the upgrade, provided Customer remains on substantially similar usage patterns as compared to the 30‑day period preceding the upgrade."

3) SLO credits cap language: "Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet agreed Service Level Objectives shall be the credits set forth in Exhibit C, subject to a cumulative cap equal to two (2) times Customer's average monthly fees during the immediately preceding three (3) month period."

4) Audit/telemetry: avoid contractual obligations to ship detailed telemetry. Instead: "Customer shall provide summary usage reports on request; Redwood will provide substantiating telemetry for incidents where credits are claimed. Disclosure of detailed telemetry shall be subject to a separate data sharing addendum."

I can prepare a tracked Word/PDF to send back to CloudNova if Connor confirms we want the 90‑day stability as the baseline. Also propose we attach a short commercial appendix that shows example scenarios and the credit calculation to avoid repeated negotiation.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
